6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.

11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.

## 1. The guests and the glad tidings  (`#the-guests-and-the-glad-tidings`)

Cited ayat: 11:69-73, 15:51-56, 51:24-30

> **11:69** وَلَقَدْ جَآءَتْ رُسُلُنَآ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ بِٱلْبُشْرَىٰ قَالُوا۟ سَلَٰمًا قَالَ سَلَٰمٌ فَمَا لَبِثَ أَن جَآءَ بِعِجْلٍ حَنِيذٍ
>
> **11:70** فَلَمَّا رَءَآ أَيْدِيَهُمْ لَا تَصِلُ إِلَيْهِ نَكِرَهُمْ وَأَوْجَسَ مِنْهُمْ خِيفَةً قَالُوا۟ لَا تَخَفْ إِنَّآ أُرْسِلْنَآ إِلَىٰ قَوْمِ لُوطٍ
>
> **11:71** وَٱمْرَأَتُهُۥ قَآئِمَةٌ فَضَحِكَتْ فَبَشَّرْنَٰهَا بِإِسْحَٰقَ وَمِن وَرَآءِ إِسْحَٰقَ يَعْقُوبَ
>
> **11:72** قَالَتْ يَٰوَيْلَتَىٰٓ ءَأَلِدُ وَأَنَا۠ عَجُوزٌ وَهَٰذَا بَعْلِى شَيْخًا إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَشَىْءٌ عَجِيبٌ
>
> **11:73** قَالُوٓا۟ أَتَعْجَبِينَ مِنْ أَمْرِ ٱللَّهِ رَحْمَتُ ٱللَّهِ وَبَرَكَٰتُهُۥ عَلَيْكُمْ أَهْلَ ٱلْبَيْتِ إِنَّهُۥ حَمِيدٌ مَّجِيدٌ

> **15:51** وَنَبِّئْهُمْ عَن ضَيْفِ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ
>
> **15:52** إِذْ دَخَلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِ فَقَالُوا۟ سَلَٰمًا قَالَ إِنَّا مِنكُمْ وَجِلُونَ
>
> **15:53** قَالُوا۟ لَا تَوْجَلْ إِنَّا نُبَشِّرُكَ بِغُلَٰمٍ عَلِيمٍ
>
> **15:54** قَالَ أَبَشَّرْتُمُونِى عَلَىٰٓ أَن مَّسَّنِىَ ٱلْكِبَرُ فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونَ
>
> **15:55** قَالُوا۟ بَشَّرْنَٰكَ بِٱلْحَقِّ فَلَا تَكُن مِّنَ ٱلْقَٰنِطِينَ
>
> **15:56** قَالَ وَمَن يَقْنَطُ مِن رَّحْمَةِ رَبِّهِۦٓ إِلَّا ٱلضَّآلُّونَ

> **51:24** هَلْ أَتَىٰكَ حَدِيثُ ضَيْفِ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ ٱلْمُكْرَمِينَ
>

>

>
> **51:27** فَقَرَّبَهُۥٓ إِلَيْهِمْ قَالَ أَلَا تَأْكُلُونَ

>
> **51:29** فَأَقْبَلَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُهُۥ فِى صَرَّةٍ فَصَكَّتْ وَجْهَهَا وَقَالَتْ عَجُوزٌ عَقِيمٌ
>
> **51:30** قَالُوا۟ كَذَٰلِكِ قَالَ رَبُّكِ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْحَكِيمُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ

### Claims

**c1** (15:51, 51:24): One passage tells the one addressed to inform people about the guests of Ibrahim, and another asks whether the account of Ibrahim's honoured guests has reached the listener.

**c2** (11:69, 15:52, 51:25): Messengers came to Ibrahim with glad tidings; they said peace, and he answered peace.

**c3** (11:69, 51:26-27): He soon brought a roasted calf, which another passage calls a fat calf; he turned quietly to his family for it, and set it near them, asking whether they would not eat.

**c4** (11:70, 51:28): When he saw that their hands did not reach it, he found them strange and felt fear of them.

**c5** (15:52): In another passage he told them that he was afraid of them.

**c6** (11:70, 15:53, 51:28): They told him not to fear: they had been sent to the people of Lut, and they gave him glad tidings of a knowing boy.

**c7** (11:71): His wife was standing there; she laughed, and they gave her glad tidings of Ishaq and, after Ishaq, of Yaqub.

**c8** (11:72): She said: woe to me, shall I give birth when I am an old woman and this husband of mine is old? This is a strange thing.

**c9** (51:29): In another passage she came forward with a cry, struck her face and said that she was an old woman, barren.

**c10** (11:73): They said: do you wonder at God's command? God's mercy and blessings are upon you, people of the house; He is praiseworthy and glorious.

**c11** (51:30): In another passage they said that it was so because her Lord had said so, and that He is the wise, the knowing.

**c12** (15:54): Ibrahim asked whether they had given him glad tidings although old age had touched him, and on what basis they gave glad tidings.

**c13** (15:55-56): They said that they had given him glad tidings in truth and that he should not be among the despairing; he said that only those who are astray despair of the mercy of their Lord.

### One-minute summary

Messengers came to Ibrahim with glad tidings, and he served them a calf [c2][c3]. They told him not to fear and gave glad tidings of a boy to him and to his wife, of Ishaq and then of Yaqub [c6][c7].

### Complete story

Messengers came to Ibrahim with glad tidings; they said peace, and he answered peace [c2]. He soon brought a roasted calf, and set it near them [c3]. When he saw that their hands did not reach it, he found them strange and felt fear of them [c4], and he told them that he was afraid [c5].

They told him not to fear: they had been sent to the people of Lut, and they gave him glad tidings of a knowing boy [c6]. His wife was standing there; she laughed, and they gave her glad tidings of Ishaq and, after Ishaq, of Yaqub [c7]. She said she was an old woman and her husband old, and called it a strange thing [c8]; in another passage she came forward with a cry, struck her face and said she was barren [c9].

The messengers asked whether she wondered at God's command, and wished mercy and blessings on the people of the house [c10]. Ibrahim asked whether they had given him glad tidings although old age had touched him [c12]. They said they had given them in truth and that he should not despair [c13], and he answered that only the astray despair of the mercy of their Lord [c13].

### Deep study

The visit is told in more than one passage, each with its own details: the roasted calf and the peace greeting [c2][c3], the fear and the words that answered it [c4][c5][c6], the glad tidings to the wife and to Ibrahim [c7][c12]. Her reaction is given in different forms [c8][c9], and so is the answer of the guests [c10][c11]. The passages also open with a call to attention [c1].

### Kids mode

Messengers came to Ibrahim with good news [c2]. He brought them a calf, but they did not eat it, and he felt afraid [c3][c4]. They told him not to be afraid and gave him good news of a boy [c6].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage joins hospitality with a surprise: the guest's food is set out before the news is given [c3][c6]. Another is that Ibrahim answers the news by saying that only the astray despair of their Lord's mercy [c13].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who the messengers were, how many they were, or what form they had; the verses call them messengers and guests only.
- Not established: where Ibrahim lived at the time, or the age of Ibrahim and his wife; the verses speak of old age but give no numbers.
- The Arabic word for her laughing (11:71) is understood in more than one way; a scholar should decide the rendering.
- The identity of the knowing boy of 15:53 and 51:28, and its relation to the glad tidings of Ishaq in 11:71, is read in more than one way; this draft does not decide.
- The wife is not named in these verses.
- The passages 11:69-73, 15:51-56 and 51:24-30 are read as one visit on matching wording (an inference).

## 2. The business of the messengers  (`#the-business-of-the-messengers`)

Cited ayat: 11:74-76, 15:57-60, 51:31-37

> **11:74** فَلَمَّا ذَهَبَ عَنْ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ ٱلرَّوْعُ وَجَآءَتْهُ ٱلْبُشْرَىٰ يُجَٰدِلُنَا فِى قَوْمِ لُوطٍ
>
> **11:75** إِنَّ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ لَحَلِيمٌ أَوَّٰهٌ مُّنِيبٌ
>
> **11:76** يَٰٓإِبْرَٰهِيمُ أَعْرِضْ عَنْ هَٰذَآ إِنَّهُۥ قَدْ جَآءَ أَمْرُ رَبِّكَ وَإِنَّهُمْ ءَاتِيهِمْ عَذَابٌ غَيْرُ مَرْدُودٍ

> **15:57** قَالَ فَمَا خَطْبُكُمْ أَيُّهَا ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ
>
> **15:58** قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّآ أُرْسِلْنَآ إِلَىٰ قَوْمٍ مُّجْرِمِينَ
>
> **15:59** إِلَّآ ءَالَ لُوطٍ إِنَّا لَمُنَجُّوهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
>
> **15:60** إِلَّا ٱمْرَأَتَهُۥ قَدَّرْنَآ إِنَّهَا لَمِنَ ٱلْغَٰبِرِينَ

> **51:31** قَالَ فَمَا خَطْبُكُمْ أَيُّهَا ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ
>
> **51:32** قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّآ أُرْسِلْنَآ إِلَىٰ قَوْمٍ مُّجْرِمِينَ
>
> **51:33** لِنُرْسِلَ عَلَيْهِمْ حِجَارَةً مِّن طِينٍ
>
> **51:34** مُّسَوَّمَةً عِندَ رَبِّكَ لِلْمُسْرِفِينَ
>
> **51:35** فَأَخْرَجْنَا مَن كَانَ فِيهَا مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
>
> **51:36** فَمَا وَجَدْنَا فِيهَا غَيْرَ بَيْتٍ مِّنَ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ
>
> **51:37** وَتَرَكْنَا فِيهَآ ءَايَةً لِّلَّذِينَ يَخَافُونَ ٱلْعَذَابَ ٱلْأَلِيمَ

### Claims

**c1** (15:57, 51:31): Ibrahim asked the messengers what their business was.

**c2** (15:58, 51:32-34): They said that they had been sent to a people of criminals, to send down on them stones of clay marked with their Lord for those who exceed all bounds.

**c3** (15:59-60): The family of Lut would be saved, all of them, except his wife, whom God had decreed to be among those who stay behind.

**c4** (11:74): When the fear had left Ibrahim and the glad tidings had come to him, he began to plead with God about the people of Lut.

**c5** (11:75): God describes Ibrahim as forbearing, awwah and turning back to Him, awwah being a word understood in more than one way.

**c6** (11:76): Ibrahim was told to turn away from this, for the command of his Lord had come and a punishment that could not be turned back was coming to them.

**c7** (51:35-36): God says that He brought out the believers who were in it, and found in it only one house of those who submitted.

**c8** (51:37): God says that He left in it a sign for those who fear the painful punishment.

### One-minute summary

Ibrahim asked the messengers what their business was, and they said they were sent to a people of criminals, but the family of Lut would be saved [c1][c2][c3]. Ibrahim pleaded with God about the people of Lut and was told to turn away from this [c4][c6].

### Complete story

Ibrahim asked the messengers what their business was [c1]. They said that they had been sent to a people of criminals, to send down on them stones of clay marked with their Lord [c2]. The family of Lut would be saved, all of them, except his wife, whom God had decreed to be among those who stay behind [c3].

When the fear had left Ibrahim and the glad tidings had come to him, he began to plead with God about the people of Lut [c4]. God describes Ibrahim as forbearing, awwah and turning back to Him [c5]. He was told to turn away from this, for the command of his Lord had come and a punishment that could not be turned back was coming to them [c6].

God says He brought out the believers who were in it and found only one house of those who submitted [c7], and that He left in it a sign for those who fear the painful punishment [c8].

### Deep study

The later part of the visit turns from the glad tidings to the sending [c1][c2]. The exception for the family of Lut and the one who stays behind [c3] is told in one passage, Ibrahim's pleading in another [c4][c5][c6], and the outcome in yet another [c7][c8]. The passages differ in what they include, and the pleading is told only in 11:74-76 [c4].

### Kids mode

Ibrahim asked the messengers why they had come [c1]. They said they were sent to a people who did wrong, but that the family of Lut would be saved [c2][c3]. Ibrahim pleaded for them, and was told to turn away from this [c4][c6].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that God's description of Ibrahim as forbearing and turning back to Him sits beside his pleading [c4][c5]. Another is that the passage records a limit: a command that had come could not be turned back [c6].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: the name of the place, how long it took, or how the believers were brought out.
- Not established: how many were in the one house of those who submitted.
- The word awwah (11:75) is rendered in different ways, for example tender-hearted or one who often calls on God; a scholar should decide.
- The wife of Lut is not named in these verses.
- The pronoun in 51:35-37, rendered 'it', refers to a place the verses do not name here.
- The inventory range stops at these ayat; the destruction itself is told elsewhere and is not part of this record.
